title: Functional switching lemma under Bernoulli restrictions
statement:
Fix an integer $n \ge 1$ and a Boolean function $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}$ whose decision-tree depth is at most $w$, for some integer $w \ge 1$. Let $p$ be a real parameter with $0 < p \le 1/(40w)$ (so in particular $p \le 1$), and draw a Bernoulli$(p)$ random restriction $\rho$ on the $n$ variables: independently, each variable is left free with probability $p$ and otherwise fixed to $0$ or to $1$, each with probability $(1-p)/2$. Then for every $t \in \bbn$, the restricted function $f\restriction\rho$ (that is, $f$ evaluated on the free coordinates with the remaining coordinates set by $\rho$) satisfies
\[
  \bbP_\rho\big[\, \text{decision-tree depth of } f\restriction\rho > t \,\big] \;\le\; \left(\tfrac12\right)^{t} + \exp\!\left(-\,\tfrac{np}{3}\right).
\]
hypotheses_covered: decision-tree depth of $f$ is at most $w$
replaced:
For any function $f$ with decision-tree depth $\le w$ (with $w > 0$, $n > 0$) and any
$0 < p \le 1/(40w)$, the Bernoulli$(p)$ restriction satisfies
$\Pr_\rho[\mathrm{dtDepth}(\mathrm{restrictFn}\, f\,\rho) > t] \le (1/2)^t + \exp(-np/3)$.
This is the switching lemma stated at the level of functions rather than formulas.
